_meta.title: Dreamers Wisdom Codex
_meta.description: Structured knowledge frameworks to power agent tooling, daily wisdom, and learning features across the Dreamers ecosystem. Sourced from owner-provided reference material (2026-08-14).
_meta.usage: Feed to QUILL/ORACLE as reference, surface as a 'Codex' dashboard section, power a daily-wisdom card, or ground the education engine.

items.name: The Growth Paradox
items.text: Growth takes much longer than you think, then happens much faster than you ever imagined.

items.name: The Persuasion Paradox
items.text: The most persuasive people don't argue — they observe, listen, and ask questions.

items.name: The Effort Paradox
items.text: You have to put in more effort to make something appear effortless.

items.name: The Wisdom Paradox
items.text: The more I learn, the more I realize how much I don't know. (Einstein)

items.name: The Productivity Paradox
items.text: Work longer, get less done.

items.name: The Speed Paradox
items.text: You have to slow down to speed up — slowing down lets you be deliberate.

items.name: The Money Paradox
items.text: You have to lose money in order to make money.

items.name: The News Paradox
items.text: The more news you consume, the less well-informed you actually are.

items.name: The Icarus Paradox
items.text: What makes you successful can lead to your downfall.

items.name: The Failure Paradox
items.text: You have to fail more to succeed more.

items.name: The Shrinking Paradox
items.text: In order to grow, sometimes you need to shrink.

items.name: The Tony Robbins Paradox
items.text: In investing, admitting you have no edge can be the ultimate edge.

items.name: The Death Paradox
items.text: Know your death in order to truly live your life.

items.name: The Say No Paradox
items.text: Take on less, accomplish more.

items.name: The Talking Paradox
items.text: Two ears, one mouth — listen twice as much as you speak. (Epictetus)

items.name: The Connectedness Paradox
items.text: More connectedness, less connected.

items.name: The Control Paradox
items.text: More controlling, less control.

items.name: The Looking Paradox
items.text: You may have to stop looking to find what you're looking for.

items.name: The Constant Change Paradox
items.text: When you are finished changing, you are finished. (Franklin)

items.name: The Fear Paradox
items.text: The thing we fear most is often the thing we need to prioritize above all else.

items.name: Deductive
items.text: From general principles to specific cases. All mammals breathe air; a whale is a mammal; a whale breathes air.

items.name: Inductive
items.text: From specific observations to general rules. The sun has risen every morning, so it always rises.

items.name: Abductive
items.text: Best explanation from incomplete data. The road is wet, so it probably rained.

items.name: Modal
items.text: Reasoning about possibility, necessity, and impossibility.

items.name: Fuzzy
items.text: Truth exists on a spectrum. The soup is 'warm', not hot or cold.

items.name: Dialectical
items.text: Ideas evolve through contradictions: thesis → antithesis → synthesis.

items.name: Informal
items.text: Everyday reasoning with claims and arguments.

thinkingBehaviours.title: 9 Thinking Behaviours (Intellectual Standards)
thinkingBehaviours.source: Richard Paul & Linda Elder, Critical Thinking (2006)

items.name: Clarity
items.prompt: Could you elaborate? Could you give an example?

items.name: Accuracy
items.prompt: How could we check that? How do we know it's true?

items.name: Precision
items.prompt: Could you be more specific / exact?

items.name: Relevance
items.prompt: How does this relate to the problem?

items.name: Depth
items.prompt: What makes this difficult? Have you predicted outcomes?

items.name: Breadth
items.prompt: Do you need to consider other points of view?

items.name: Logic
items.prompt: Does this make sense together? Does it follow the evidence?

items.name: Fairness
items.prompt: Am I considering the thinking of others? Is my purpose fair?

items.name: Significance
items.prompt: Which of these facts are the most important?
